items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Toby, he's dead now -- very dear friend.

ctx.x: You know how guys stand on the corner. He was standing on the corner, him and Claude Hopkins, Toby "Otto" Hardwick, standing on the corner, they was talking some jive, so Toby, he's dead now -- very dear friend. They started talking about New York. He said, "Sonny, can tell you about New York." He's from New York. So I come in there and started that jive talk, that old funny talk, telling them cats about New York, painting a glorious picture about New York, and right away them cats they was on me like white on…

I was a charter member then and Duke played piano then, but he had a diploma from the University, from Howard University, commercial illustrator, you know paint them pictures, and he wasn't thinking about becoming no professional. He used to play around at houseparties, and clubs or something like that, but he wasn't playing that no mind. Playing music was the furtherest; but Toby could play, He played saxophone and bass, and he was so small, a lot of times his older brother used to have to carry the bass for…
